evidence.claim: The World Bank approved a US$500 million project to keep poor and vulnerable Egyptian households supplied with bread, cushion Ukraine-war price shocks, and support food-security reforms; it tied the project to Egypt's Bread Subsidy Program and about one month of wheat supply for roughly 70 million low-income Egyptians, including about 31 million people under the poverty line.
evidence.title: US$ 500 Million Project Will Help to Strengthen Egypt's Food and Nutrition Security
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank approved a US$500 million project to keep poor and vulnerable Egyptian households supplied with bread, cushion Ukraine-war price shocks, and support food-security reforms; it tied the project to Egypt's Bread Subsidy Program and about one month of wheat supply for roughly 70 million low-income Egyptians, including about 31 million people under the poverty line.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous World Bank press release with specific project terms, beneficiary counts, and policy rationale.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Sisi government as the borrower-side authority and policy sponsor, though the shock context was heavily external.
contrary_evidence: The project is a response to crisis pressure, not proof of structural welfare improvement by year-end.
The same text emphasizes pandemic and Ukraine-war shocks.

evidence.claim: The World Bank announced US$500 million to expand Egypt's Takaful and Karama program, saying it covered 3.69 million households as of June 2022, that women were 74 percent of card holders/direct beneficiaries, and that 67 percent of the cash went to Upper Egypt.
evidence.title: New World Bank Financing Will Expand and Strengthen Egypt's Flagship Social Protection Program
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank announced US$500 million to expand Egypt's Takaful and Karama program, saying it covered 3.69 million households as of June 2022, that women were 74 percent of card holders/direct beneficiaries, and that 67 percent of the cash went to Upper Egypt.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank press release with direct coverage, targeting, and distribution details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Sisi government as the policy sponsor, though co-designed with the World Bank and focused on implementation through the Ministry of Social Solidarity.
contrary_evidence: This shows mitigation and targeting, not a full answer to poverty or labor-market weakness.
It does not prove that vulnerable households were adequately protected from inflation.

evidence.claim: UNICEF said marginalized children, especially migrant and refugee children, were below expected learning levels in literacy and numeracy after COVID-19, and that UNICEF was working with Egypt's education ministry and partners to reach close to 30,000 children with a remediation programme and assessment tools.
evidence.title: Recovering from COVID-19 Learning Losses
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF said marginalized children, especially migrant and refugee children, were below expected learning levels in literacy and numeracy after COVID-19, and that UNICEF was working with Egypt's education ministry and partners to reach close to 30,000 children with a remediation programme and assessment tools.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous UNICEF country story with explicit Egypt-specific remedial action and target group descriptions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the national education system under the Sisi government, but the remedial action was jointly implemented with UNICEF and external donors.
contrary_evidence: The story emphasizes learning loss and unequal access rather than a completed recovery.
It is a program description, not a final outcome evaluation.

evidence.claim: WHO and Egypt's Ministry of Health held a 2022 conference for 200 primary health-care workers and said family physicians are the first point of contact for essential care and health emergencies, while WHO continued technical and capacity-building support for family medicine.
evidence.title: WHO Egypt and Ministry of Health and Population celebrate physicians on Family Doctor Day
evidence.excerpt: WHO and Egypt's Ministry of Health held a 2022 conference for 200 primary health-care workers and said family physicians are the first point of contact for essential care and health emergencies, while WHO continued technical and capacity-building support for family medicine.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous WHO country-office report on a concrete 2022 event and support activity.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Ministry of Health under the Sisi government, though the source also reflects WHO and USAID support.
contrary_evidence: A conference and training support do not prove system-wide service quality.
The source emphasizes staffing shortages and the need for further investment.

evidence.claim: WHO said it worked with Egyptian health authorities in August 2022 to develop the national strategic plan for the hospital sector, and that Egypt was taking active steps to implement universal health insurance and build a more resilient health system.
evidence.title: WHO Egypt works towards improving the hospital sector in Egypt
evidence.excerpt: WHO said it worked with Egyptian health authorities in August 2022 to develop the national strategic plan for the hospital sector, and that Egypt was taking active steps to implement universal health insurance and build a more resilient health system.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous WHO country-office report describing a specific policy workshop and the government's UHI implementation direction.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Sisi-era health ministry and linked institutions, though implementation was collaborative with WHO and higher-education bodies.
contrary_evidence: The source is a workshop report, not an outcome evaluation.
It notes system-development challenges rather than completed reform.

evidence.claim: Egypt signed a CHF 7.2 million grant on 10 February 2022 for an Aswan water project under SDG 6, with related goals of good health and reduced inequalities.
evidence.title: Improving Wastewater Services Program - Upper Egypt
evidence.excerpt: Egypt signed a CHF 7.2 million grant on 10 February 2022 for an Aswan water project under SDG 6, with related goals of good health and reduced inequalities.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official ministry project page with a dated financing agreement and explicit location/objective information.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Sisi government through its international-cooperation ministry, though the project was donor-financed and locally implemented.
contrary_evidence: The page gives project metadata rather than completion or impact results.
It is a grant announcement, not an implementation audit.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said its rural sanitation program for Egypt aimed to increase access to and services of rural sanitation in Beheira, Dakahliya, and Sharkiya, improving citizens' well-being and protecting agricultural soil.
evidence.title: Sustainable Rural Sanitation Services Program for Egypt
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said its rural sanitation program for Egypt aimed to increase access to and services of rural sanitation in Beheira, Dakahliya, and Sharkiya, improving citizens' well-being and protecting agricultural soil.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Dated World Bank project infographic with explicit geography and objective.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the broader Sisi-era state program and its development partners, not to a single ministerial decision.
contrary_evidence: The infographic is a goal statement, not proof of finished service expansion in 2022.
It does not quantify completed households or outcomes.

unresolved_gaps: There is no direct 2022 ruler-attributed nuclear command, safety, or crisis decision in the file.
El Dabaa evidence is mostly permits, construction milestones, and project self-reporting, not independent safety enforcement.
The package shows mediation and diplomatic statements, but not the internal decision chain or independent proof that Egypt's mediation changed outcomes.
There is little direct evidence on any offensive military option or coercive-force decision in 2022.
The chain from abuse to personal or cabinet-level accountability is thin, especially for prisons, police, and protest repression.
The limited remedial evidence is not outcome-verified; pardons and release gestures need follow-through data.
There was no live national election in 2022, so contestability and succession are inferred largely from retrospective rights reporting.
The internal effect of dialogue initiatives and jail releases on pluralism is not independently shown.
Hard verification of State Ownership Policy implementation and actual divestments by year-end is thin.
Household-level welfare effects of inflation, transfers, and bread security are incompletely tied to ruler action.
The package lacks direct ruler-level attribution for social-welfare decisions beyond ministerial and partner-mediated actions.
There is little completed-outcome evidence for 2022 on poverty, learning loss, malnutrition, and sanitation after the interventions.
Direct evidence of personal assets, beneficial ownership, procurement gains, or family enrichment is still missing.
The file has one clear public denial and several propaganda or censorship claims, but fewer independently verified false statements with explicit contradiction.
The core 2022 economic program is reconstructed from speeches, policy papers, and partial implementation steps rather than a single explicit governing program document.
Independent verification of divestment, budget execution, and durable follow-through is still thin.
